reviewKind: O1-p r2 product unit plus inventory v141

closedFindings.assessment: After the existing fixed-fd type, access and FD_CLOEXEC checks, F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC creates a fresh descriptor. Only that successful duplicate is passed to File::from_raw_fd. Descriptor 3 remains open and unowned by admission, and all failure paths create no File owner. The updated test verifies distinct close-on-exec duplicates, repeated admission and writes after dropping the first owner. An independent safe-Rust child also verifies overlap with an existing File owner of descriptor 3 and forced reuse of the first duplicate.

The Into<i64> helper uses identity/infallible widening for the supported signed libc timeval fields. Range::contains preserves rejection of negative or million-microsecond observations. The failed-getrusage typed path and checked user-plus-system duration remain intact. All six focused serial controls and warning-denied all-targets clippy pass on pinned macOS Rust 1.95.0.

inventoryCandidateAssessment.assessment: Inventory v141 and its successor record are byte-for-byte unchanged from the accepted r1 assessment. The three added platform rows still describe this corrected implementation. All 1012 parent rows, package graph and pending decisions are preserved; all 913 tracked/intent-to-add files are covered. All 103 effective descriptions and selectors match the unchanged selected-v140 inheritance, including 79 selector movements. Both carried unresolved obligations remain unresolved.

addedRowsByValue.description: Consume a Result under a closed Disposition and do nothing else. No record, no I/O and no allocation; O1-S moves call sites onto it.
Construct the TestOnly and ShutdownPath dispositions. Compiled only for tests; confers no qualification.
Admit inherited descriptor 3 when it is a writable FIFO or regular file, then set close-on-exec. A closed, read-only or other descriptor is refused unowned.

reviewOperations.cargo: All three cargo invocations used --locked --offline, the pinned toolchain, and a private TMPDIR/target directory. Each acquired the shared lane lock through its own mkdir and removed only that owned lock immediately after its child exited. The waiting process argv contained no cargo text.
